name: Akumuli
tagline: Single-node C++ time-series database with a hybrid LSM/B+tree engine and strong compression; archived.
description: Akumuli is a time-series database written in C++ by Eugene Lazin, designed to get very high write throughput out of one machine with SSD or NVMe storage. Its NB+tree storage engine mixes LSM and B+tree ideas with MVCC, compresses values better than Facebook's Gorilla scheme, and can aggregate or downsample without pre-configured rollups; queries are JSON over HTTP and ingestion accepts OpenTSDB's telnet-style protocol, so collectors such as collectd and netdata work unchanged. It could also run embedded as a library, and a Grafana datasource existed. The last release was v0.8.80 in May 2020 and the GitHub repository is now archived, so it is a source of design ideas rather than something to deploy.
statusNote: GitHub repository archived; last release v0.8.80 (May 2020). Use VictoriaMetrics, QuestDB or TimescaleDB instead.

scale.notes: Scales up across cores on one server; benchmarks claimed millions of writes per second on a single box. No clustering.

strengths: Very high single-node ingest rates on SSD/NVMe
Compression ratio that beat the Gorilla scheme in the author's tests
Downsampling and aggregation without pre-defined rollups
Can be embedded as a library as well as run as a server
weaknesses: Repository archived; no fixes or releases since 2020
JSON query API instead of SQL or PromQL limits tool support
Small user base and few integrations beyond Grafana
useCases: Studying time-series storage engine and compression design
Existing single-node metrics deployments that already run it
